Classic Independence Day Beef Burgers

Served at: Independence Day (United States)

Serves 4Prep 15 minutesCook 10-15 minutes

Burgers are a quintessential American dish, especially beloved for summer gatherings and patriotic holidays. On Independence Day, sizzling burgers on the grill are a symbol of casual celebration, bringing families and friends together for a festive meal under the summer sky. This recipe focuses on simple, flavorful beef patties, perfect for customizing with your favorite toppings.

Ingredients

  • 1.5 pounds (680 grams) ground beef, 80/20 chuck
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 0.5 teaspoon black pepper
  • 0.5 teaspoon onion powder (optional)
  • 0.25 teaspoon garlic powder (optional)
  • 4 burger buns, split
  • 4 slices cheese (Cheddar, American, or Monterey Jack)
  • 4 lettuce leaves
  • 1 large tomato, sliced
  • 0.5 red onion, thinly sliced
  • 4 dill pickle slices
  • Ketchup, for serving
  • Mustard, for serving
  • Mayonnaise, for serving

Method

  1. In a large bowl, gently combine the ground beef with salt, black pepper, onion powder (if using), and garlic powder (if using). Avoid overmixing, as this can make the burgers tough.
  2. Divide the meat mixture into four equal portions and gently form each into a 0.75-inch (2 cm) thick patty. Make a slight indentation in the center of each patty with your thumb to prevent it from bulging during cooking.
  3. Preheat your grill to medium-high heat (about 400°F or 200°C). Lightly oil the grill grates.
  4. Place the patties on the hot grill. Cook for 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, 5-6 minutes per side for medium, or longer for well-done, flipping only once.
  5. During the last minute of cooking, place a slice of cheese on each patty to melt.
  6. While the burgers are cooking, lightly toast the burger buns on the grill or in a toaster until golden.
  7. Assemble the burgers: spread desired condiments on the toasted buns, then add a lettuce leaf, tomato slice, onion slice, and pickle slices.
  8. Place a cheesy burger patty on top of the vegetables and cover with the top bun. Serve immediately.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, add a dash of Worcestershire sauce or a spoonful of finely minced onion to the ground beef mixture.
  • To prevent sticking, ensure your grill grates are clean and well-oiled before placing the patties.
  • Experiment with different cheeses and toppings like bacon, sautéed mushrooms, or avocado to customize your burgers.
